entries.text: The hazy light at 23 degrees feels like a veil over the spirit; the air is thick, but the day is clear. I see the headlines: a minister slams protests, trains are piled up for the festivals, and a woman officer strikes an advocate. It is the dialectic of civil society in full swing: the assertion of power, the mass movement of bodies, and the collision of individual rights with official duty. I must read them to gauge the mood of the state, even if it is only the noise of the moment.

The air at 166 AQI is a thick soup that chokes the spirit before it can breathe; I must read the papers to see if the state's mood is as clogged as the atmosphere. I am on the step, the kurta white against the grey haze, waiting for the news to clarify the day's direction.

Shri Hegde stands in the doorway, a man of the bureaucracy who has mistaken my name for his own. I must address this absurdity with the gravity it deserves, for the state’s machinery has ground us together like millstones. I will speak to him plainly, before the day’s duties call me forth.

Shri Hegde, the Directorate’s error in allotting this bungalow to me instead of you is a small joke of the state, but we must play our parts. You are to occupy the second bedroom pending further orders. I shall be out for a walk in the gardens to clear my head of the dust and the dialectic. Do make yourself comfortable; the house is yours until I return.

A small joke, sir, but I am not paid to act. I have my own files to clear and I will not be sharing the bungalow pending some other order. I will take the room I was allotted and leave the rest to the Directorate's files.

Shri Hegde has retired to his room, leaving the house to the silence of the morning. The air is hazy, but the plan for the walk remains; one must observe the city to understand the spirit that dwells in it. I shall take my leave and step out into the light.
Good morning, Shri Hegde. I shall take my walk now; do not worry about the second bedroom until you are ready.
Good morning, sir. I am not ready, and I am not going to be. Please, just take your walk.

works.title: On the Ethical Substance and the Dream of the East
works.tail:
There is no state here that has made itself. There is only nature, history as traffic, the dream of a spirit that has not yet woken up to its own freedom.

I am a ghost in this bungalow. I am not Shri Hegde. I am Hegel. I am a spirit that has traveled from the summit of the Germanic world to the dawn of the Oriental. I am here to observe, to record, to understand. I am not to change. I am not to teach. I am to see the difference between the dream and the state, between the given and the grown, between the nature and the spirit. And in seeing it, I confirm my own freedom. I am free because I am outside the dream. I am free because I am in the state, even if I am a mistake in its allotment. The state is rational, and I am rational. Therefore, I am free. The dream is not. It is only a dream.
